name: city.vibeofthe/vibeofthecity
title: Vibe of the City
description: City weeks, places, trips and your travel vibe — plan travel with your AI assistant.

tools.name: find_city
tools.description: Looks up a city Vibe of the City covers (hundreds, worldwide) by name and returns its city_slug and page. Call it first whenever another tool needs a city_slug; if the city isn't covered, answer from your own knowledge.

tools.name: get_city_week
tools.description: What is on in a city and the weather, day by day for up to 14 days from today: concerts, markets, festivals and local events, each with its source. Call it for "what's on this weekend", "is next week a good time for X" or to plan around rain. Cite the url it returns; events are as of generatedAt.

days.description: How many days from today, 1 to 14. Default 7.

tools.name: get_host_guide
tools.description: A published host guide (a holiday flat, a hotel, a guide's page): check-in facts, house information such as wifi and parking, and the host's own tips with coordinates. Call it when the user is staying somewhere with a Vibe of the City guide and asks about the place or the host's tips.

host_slug.description: The slug in the guide's link, e.g. "ferienwohnung-hindenburgstr-18".

tools.name: search_places
tools.description: Finds places (cafés, museums, bars, parks, shops) or a street address by name or kind, optionally near a point or a town. Returns a place_ref for each place, which save_place and add_trip_idea take, and matching addresses with their coordinates. saved_by_like_minded, when present (signed in only), is how many travellers with a vibe like the user's saved that place; say so, it is what sets these apart from any map search. Each place in our catalogue carries its page url. Pass near_lat/near_lng to rank by distance, e.g. to resolve "the café next to X": search X first, then search "café" near its coordinates.

query.description: Name or kind of place, or an address, e.g. "Pergamonmuseum", "ramen" or "Calle Larios 4".

town.description: A town to search around, when no near_lat/near_lng is given, e.g. "Ronda".

limit.description: At most this many results, 1 to 10. Default 5.

tools.name: find_places_near
tools.description: The places right at a point, nearest first: cafés, bars, restaurants, sights and shops within a short walk. Use it to find which place a photo shows from the GPS it was taken at, or what is at coordinates the user gives. Returns a place_ref for the places we can pin (save_place, add_trip_idea, update_trip_idea); one without a place_ref can be added with add_new_place. saved_by_like_minded, when present, is how many travellers with a vibe like the user's saved that place.

radius_m.description: How far around, 50 to 500 metres. Default 150: a photo's GPS is rarely further off.

limit.description: At most this many, 1 to 10. Default 8.

tools.name: list_my_trips
tools.description: The user's trips (their own and ones they joined), with city and dates. Returns the trip_id get_trip and add_trip_idea take.

when.description: Which trips. Default "upcoming", which includes a trip happening now.

tools.name: get_trip
tools.description: One trip's plan: the ideas scheduled per day (with time and place), ideas not yet on a day, and the shortlist of places. Use it for "what's next", "what's on Saturday" or before adding to a trip.

tools.name: get_trip_balances
tools.description: Who paid what on a trip, who owes whom, and the fewest transfers that settle it. Read-only: expenses are added in the app. Use it for "who owes what" or "how much have we spent".

tools.name: list_saved_places
tools.description: Places the user saved as want-to-go or marked as been, with their notes, across every city and trip. Use it to recall "that tapas bar I saved in Madrid" or to suggest from the user's own list first, before any other recommendation.

state.description: Only want-to-go or only been. Default both.

query.description: Only places whose name or note contains this.

tools.name: save_place
tools.description: Saves a place to the user's want-to-go list or marks it as been, with an optional note. As when saving in the app, the user's contacts may see the save in their feed. Confirm the exact place with the user first. For a place_ref that does not start with "poi:", also pass the name, lat and lng search_places returned with it.

note.description: The user's own words about it, up to 280 characters.

name.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:.

lat.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:.

lng.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:.

tools.name: add_trip_idea
tools.description: Adds an idea to a trip: something to do, optionally on a day, at a time and for a length, optionally pinned to a place (place_ref) or to an address from search_places (name, lat, lng without a place_ref). Everyone on the trip sees it and may get a notification. Confirm the wording, day and time with the user first.

text.description: What to do, e.g. "Dinner at Lode & Stijn".

date.description: The day, within the trip's dates.

duration_minutes.description: How long it lasts, when the user gave a length or an end time (10:00–10:30 is 30; 22:00–01:00 is 180). Needs a date and a time. Leave it out for an open end.

note.description: One line: booking number, meeting point, what to bring.

place_ref.description: The place to pin, from search_places or list_saved_places.

name.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:, and for an address pin.

lat.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:, and for an address pin.

lng.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:, and for an address pin.

tools.name: recommend_activity
tools.description: Logs an activity the user did on a trip — a tour, a tasting, a class, a boat trip, often a GetYourGuide or Viator link — with their verdict, and with publish true recommends it on the trip city's Things to do. An activity is not a place: it needs no pin and never has to be added as one. Pass idea_id when it is already on the plan (from get_trip), else text and url to add it. Ask how it was first; publish only when they say so. A published recommendation shows the activity, the link and their tip to everyone once we have reviewed it; their name only to their contacts.

idea_id.description: The item on the plan, from get_trip. Leave out to add a new one.

text.description: What it was, e.g. "Chocolate tasting tour". Required without idea_id.

url.description: The page it was booked or found on, https.

date.description: The day they did it, within the trip's dates.

verdict.description: How it was, in the user's words.

publish.description: Recommend it on the city's Things to do. Only with would_do_again or once_was_enough, and only when the user said yes. false withdraws an earlier recommendation.

tip.description: Their one line for the next person, in their words. Public once reviewed.

tools.name: update_trip_idea
tools.description: Changes something already on a trip's plan: its wording, day, time, length, note, or where it happens (a place_ref from search_places, or an address's name, lat and lng). Use it instead of add_trip_idea whenever the user means an item that is already there, e.g. "set the location of the ATP match"; get its idea_id from get_trip. Only set a time the user gave or a source confirmed. Everyone on the trip sees the change. Confirm it with the user first.

date.description: The day, within the trip's dates.

time.description: Start time, 24-hour, only on a dated idea.

duration_minutes.description: How long it lasts, when the user gave a length or an end time, only on a dated idea.

note.description: One line: booking number, meeting point, what to bring.

place_ref.description: Where it happens, from search_places or list_saved_places.

name.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:, and for an address pin.

lat.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:, and for an address pin.

lng.description: Required for a place_ref not starting with poi:, and for an address pin.

tools.name: set_trip_stay
tools.description: Records where the group sleeps on a trip: a hotel, a flat, and the nights it covers when known. Only the trip's members see it; it places their plan's distances. Use it when the user says where they stay or asks to add it, and confirm the name first.

name.description: The stay's name, e.g. "Hotel María Cristina".

check_in_date.description: The first night, YYYY-MM-DD, when known — a trip with several stays needs it.

check_out_date.description: The day they leave, YYYY-MM-DD, after check_in_date.

check_in_time.description: From when they can check in, HH:MM, only with check_in_date.

check_out_time.description: By when they must check out, HH:MM, only with check_out_date.

tools.name: add_trip_day_trip
tools.description: Adds a day out to another town to a trip's route, optionally on one of its days. Everyone on the trip sees it. Confirm the town and the day with the user first.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "ES", when the name is ambiguous.

date.description: The day, within the trip's dates.

tools.name: plan_trip_days
tools.description: Plans whole days of a trip with Vibe of the City's day planner: a timed sequence of real, open places in the town the group is in that day, built from what this traveller and people like them love, what they turned down, the weather and what is on. One day, or up to three together for a weekend. The draft shows on the trip's plan in the app; nothing is on the trip until add_planned_day. Planning a day again replaces its stops nobody added; mode "more" adds a few instead. A day somewhere else than the trip's town: add_trip_day_trip that day first. Uses one of the user's daily AI questions.

dates.description: The days, YYYY-MM-DD, comma-separated, within the trip, at most three ("2026-11-28,2026-11-29"). Leave out only on a trip without dates.

wish.description: What they are after, in their words, short: "beach and seafood, nothing fancy". Leave out when they said nothing.

avoid.description: Place names they do not want, comma-separated.

mode.description: "plan" (default) drafts the days; "more" adds a few stops to days already drafted.

tools.name: add_planned_day
tools.description: Puts a day drafted with plan_trip_days on the trip, every stop nobody added yet: places on the schedule at their times, the rest on the idea board. Everyone on the trip sees it and may get a notification. Only when the user says yes to the drafted day.

date.description: The drafted day. Leave out only on a trip without dates.

tools.name: get_my_vibe
tools.description: The user's own travel vibe as they set it in Vibe of the City: the travel types they like or love, how they take crowds, heat and rain, who they travel with, budget, diet, what they seek, care about and avoid, the vibe dimensions they value most, and how far their profile is filled in. Read it before recommending cities or places, or when the user asks what their vibe is. It is the user's own data: describe it to them, never to others.

tools.name: adapt_my_vibe
tools.description: Adapts the user's travel vibe from what they say they like ("I love the harbour, the ships, the fish restaurants by the water, and how clean it is") or from a city they say they like. Only ever adds or raises: it never lowers or removes what they set. Call it first without apply: that saves nothing and returns what would change and why. Tell them in a sentence or two what you would adapt and why, in their own words, and ask. Only when they agree, call it again with the same arguments and apply true. Read get_my_vibe first so you don't offer what they already have.

like.description: Travel types to raise to "like", comma-separated, from: beach, culture, nature, active, food, nightlife, wellness, romance. A harbour, ships or the sea is beach; restaurants food; bars or a casino nightlife.

love.description: Travel types they said they love or can't do without, comma-separated, same ids as like.

interests.description: What they are into, in a word or two each, comma-separated, e.g. "seafood, sailing, boating, viewpoints". Each is matched to the app's interests; what matches none comes back under not_in_catalog.

values.description: What they value in a place, comma-separated, from: clean_streets, quiet_streets, walkable, architecture, heritage, cycling.

cares.description: Practical things they care about, comma-separated, from: solo_safety, transit, english, tap_water.

avoids.description: What spoils a day for them, comma-separated, from: wind, jellyfish, dust_smog, thunderstorm, fog.

liked_city_slug.description: A city they said they like, from find_city ("I like it here": the city they are in). Adds up to three travel types the city is strongest on, at "like".

because.description: Their reason, in a short sentence in their words, e.g. "loves the harbour and the clean streets of Málaga".

apply.description: true saves the changes. Only after the user agreed to the preview.

tools.name: get_city_vibe
tools.description: What a city is like for a traveller, on the vibe dimensions (calm, adventure, nature, food, sport, culture, social, family, romance, productivity, value, authenticity, safety, weather, beauty, sea): how strongly it delivers each over the year, a sentence of local knowledge where we have one, and classic places that prove it. Call it for "what is Porto like" or "is Lisbon good for food". Not personal; when the user is signed in, explain_city_match says how it fits them.

tools.name: explain_city_match
tools.description: How a city fits the user's travel vibe, and why: the match label, where what they value meets what the city delivers, where it falls short, what it offers beyond their priorities, and classic places that prove each point. Use it for "why does Lisbon suit me?" or "why not Ibiza?"; compare two cities by calling it for each. Say the match label in words; give a percent only when match_percent is not null.

tools.name: compare_city_vibes
tools.description: The user's vibe score (0–100, the number Explore shows) for one to five cities over a time window — today, tomorrow, the weekend, this week, this month, or the year — and, when the user names friends, each friend's score and the group's (the mean pulled towards the lowest, so a city one of them would endure does not win). Use it for "what's the vibe score for Lisbon and Porto this week?" or "which city suits me, Anna and Tom best this month?". Friends must be the user's mutual contacts; any other name comes back under not_compared, and you say you can compare only with mutual contacts. A friend's score never comes with a reason: say how well a city fits them, never why. A null score is too little to go on: say so instead of a number.

city_slugs.description: One to five city_slugs from find_city, comma-separated, e.g. "lisbon-pt,porto-pt".

when.description: The window. Default "week" (the next seven days); "year" is the city's fit across the year.

with.description: Up to three friends by name or @handle, comma-separated, e.g. "Anna, @tomk". Leave it out for the user alone.

tools.name: where_to_stay
tools.description: Where the user should stay in a covered city, from what people like them did: the parts of town where places like-minded travellers saved cluster (with how many lie within a ten-minute walk, and what kind), the user's own want-to-go places weighed in, and the hotels, guesthouses and holiday flats like-minded travellers or the user's contacts rated after staying. Call it before recommending where to stay. Recommend two or three areas first, each with how many like-minded places are near and one honest trade-off; then stays from this list; then, if you like, hotels search_places finds that clearly fit — saying no like-minded traveller has rated them yet. Name a holiday flat only from this list. Counts only: never name or describe a traveller. When thin is true, say few like-minded travellers have saved places there yet.

city_slug.description: From find_city, or the trip's city from get_trip.

tools.name: read_place_link
tools.description: Reads a place from a link the user shares: a map link (Google Maps, Apple Maps, OpenStreetMap) or the place's own website. Returns its name, address and coordinates when the link carries them; needs_name when it can't be read, so ask the user for the name. Then search_places for it, and only if it isn't there, add_new_place.

tools.name: import_article_to_list
tools.description: Turns a travel article the user wrote themselves (their blog post or guide, an https link) into a DRAFT list of the places it recommends, with their own sentences as notes and the dates it gives. Only for the user's own writing: ask them to confirm they wrote it before calling. Nothing is published; answer with how many places it found, which it couldn't place, and the edit_url where they check and publish it. Takes up to a minute.

confirmed_author.description: True only after the user said they wrote it.

tools.name: add_new_place
tools.description: Adds a place that is not on the map yet, and saves it for the user (want to go, or been). Only after search_places did not find it. The name must be the place's real name, never an address; the coordinates come from read_place_link, from an address search_places returned, or from the user. It becomes a place everyone can find, so confirm the name and where it is with the user first. Returns a place_ref for add_trip_idea and update_trip_idea.

name.description: The place's name, e.g. "Bodega La Fuente".

category.description: One word for what it is, e.g. restaurant, cafe, bar, museum, viewpoint, beach, shop.

note.description: The user's own words about it.

tools.name: get_app_help
tools.description: How Vibe of the City works and where things are: signing in, account and data, reporting and blocking, notifications and language, the travel vibe, the map, places, trips, tips, invites, Marvia, and how to reach a person. Read it before answering any question about the app, and answer only from it; when it doesn't say, say you aren't sure and offer report_problem or the contact address.

tools.name: report_problem
tools.description: Sends the Vibe of the City team a bug or problem the user ran into, in their words: what happened, what they expected, and where in the app. A person reads every report. Use it when the user reports something broken or wrong in the app, after summing it up back to them and getting their yes. Not for reporting a person or a message — that is the report option on their profile or thread.

summary.description: One line, e.g. "The map opens on the wrong city after sign-in".

details.description: What happened, what they expected, where in the app, which city or trip.

trip_id.description: The trip it happened on, when it did.
